title: Add per-invocation liveness metrics and alert debouncing
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds per-invocation liveness counters and a configurable alert debouncer to reduce SLO noise. Includes Grafana panels and an opt-in Helm flag. No breaking API changes.
description:
Context: We see intermittent flapping of SLO alerts driven by very short-lived invocation spikes (typically <250ms) that inflate token latency percentiles for a tiny subset of requests. These spikes often correlate with transient infra hiccups (node preemption, brief cold starts) and create alert noise that distracts on-call.

Problem: Existing per-route percentiles and token-level rollups are valuable but noisy for very short bursts; SLO alerts fire even when the bulk of traffic is healthy. We need a low-risk server-side approach to (1) surface per-invocation liveness for diagnostic correlation and (2) debounce alerts so short bursts don't immediately escalate.

Proposal: 1) Add a per-invocation liveness counter that increments at key lifecycle checkpoints (accept->start->first-token->complete). These counters are exported as low-cardinality metrics that can be correlated with traces and token cost metrics. 2) Introduce an alert debouncing layer that can be configured per-SLO: short grace window (default 45s) + rolling evaluation of sustained breach. Debouncer is configurable via Helm/values and the Console.

Implementation summary: - instrumentation: pkg/serving/liveness.go implements counters and tags (route_id, model, tenant_tier) with lightweight cardinality controls; uses existing metrics emitter (metrics/v2). - debouncer: observability/alerts/debouncer.go provides in-memory sliding window logic with optional persistent state using Redis when running in Dedicated/Private. - config: charts/redwood/values.yaml adds observability.alertDebouncer with sensible defaults (enabled: true, window_seconds: 45, min_breach_ratio: 0.6). - dashboards: observability/grafana/invocation_liveness_panel.json (new panel showing per-invocation state transitions, latched breach timeline). - tests: unit tests for counter transitions and debouncer policy; integration job that runs against a synthetic load generator that produces short spikes.

Testing and results: Unit tests: 34 new tests, all passing in CI. Integration: synthetic run (100k invocations with 1% short spikes) reduced alert count by 78% while preserving true positive firings in a controlled failure. CPU/memory increase negligible (~0.8% p95).

Rollout plan: - Canary: enable on staging and 10% of production routes for 24h, monitor invocation_liveness and alert counts. - Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with k-safety rollback if false negatives detected. - Console: add toggle in Alerts UI (behind feature flag) to allow SREs and tenants to tune local debouncer settings.

Rollback: Helm toggle to disable observability.alertDebouncer; remove debouncer state in Redis if used (script provided in observability/scripts/clear_debouncer_state.sh).

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps metrics low-cardinality by aggregating liveness states rather than per-invocation IDs. Trace correlation is added via a stable tag on the invocation to the existing tracing span (trace_id is unchanged).
